claims.claim: Nie traktuj jednej godziny jako naukowo ustalonej granicy dla wszystkich urządzeń.
claims.reason: The sentence says that no one-hour (or other) threshold is scientifically established for all devices, i.e. a statement about the state of the evidence across devices. Neither cited snapshot says this. The NHS page (main region, read in full) gives an hour only as general relaxing advice (line 107, 'relax at least 1 hour before bed') and for devices says only 'right before going to bed' (line 123) with no statement about whether any threshold is evidence-based. The Chang abstract mentions '1 h' only as a survey of device use before bedtime and does not test or discuss a timing threshold. The claim goes beyond what these two sources address; it is not contradicted either. The NHS page speaks on timing, so this is unsupported rather than not_checkable.

quotes.text: Chang AM, Aeschbach D, Duffy JF, Czeisler CA.
Here we compare the biological effects of reading an electronic book on a light-emitting device (LE-eBook) with reading a printed book in the hours before bedtime.

claims.reason: Authorship (Chang first author, with co-authors) and that the authors made the comparison are in the snapshot. Part of a sentence split in three because the number 12 cannot be quoted from the snapshot.

The snapshot is the Europe PMC abstract only. It gives no sample size and no description of the participants (health status, age). The abstract mentions only a survey of 1,508 American adults, which is background and not the study sample. The full text (Methods, Participants) would be needed.

claims.reason: The wording 'Participants reading an LE-eBook ... than when reading a printed book' implies that the same participants were compared under both conditions (consistent with a crossover design). The abstract does not use the words crossover or randomised and does not say how conditions were allocated or ordered. Randomisation and the crossover label need the full text (Methods).

scope_gaps.note: The source compared reading on a light-emitting e-reader (LE-eBook) with a printed book. The sentence says 'Warunek ekranu'; a reader might assume the result applies to any screen, phone or content. The sentence does not say so, and Ograniczenia#1 flags it.
Sample size (12) and population (healthy young adults) are not in the abstract.
Randomisation and the crossover label are not stated in the abstract; only a within-participant comparison is implied.
Session length and number of evenings are not in the abstract.

The sentence makes a statement about the evidence for any one-hour boundary across all devices; the NHS page gives an hour only as general relaxing advice and neither source addresses thresholds for devices.
Design label, sample size and laboratory setting are described beyond what the abstract states.
Exposure level, setting and the authors' own view on generalisation are not in the abstract.
